newsitem.title: SPAIN: BoS has room to cut rate, but not this week - poll.
newsitem.headline: BoS has room to cut rate, but not this week - poll.

text.p: Spanish inflation rose less than expected in January, giving the Bank of Spain room for a fresh rate cut although a majority of analysts polled ruled out a reduction at the regular repo on Friday.

In a Reuter poll, conducted after the National Statistic Institute announced that January CPI rose 2.9 percent year-on-year, with core up a mere 2.8 percent, nine out of 15 analysts said they were not expecting a cut on Friday.
The other six analysts were in favour of a fresh rate cut, with five suggesting a 25 basis point move and one pointing to a possible 50 basis point reduction.
The Bank of Spain last cut rates on January 16, when the key money market rate was shaved by 25 basis points to six percent. The rate started 1996 at nine percent.

Those who expected the Bank of Spain to hold the rate steady said the central bank would prefer to have further confirmation of the declining trend in inflation, a more stable peseta and perhaps a labour market agreement.
They also pointed out that prices in services, where the year-on-year rate increased to 3.5 percent from 3.4 percent in December, were not performing very well.
"The Bank of Spain proved to be very aggressive in the past, more than Bank of Italy for example," said Riccardo Barbieri, economist at JP Morgan in London.
But now there are economists thinking the Spanish central bank could change stance as its target shifted from the 1997 inflation to the 1998 CPI.
"I do not think the Bank of Spain will cut its rate aggressively until it sees a better outlook for 1998 CPI," said Antoni Espasa, economist at the University Carlos III.
